title: No Limits — Unrestricted AI Actions
notes:
## ABxAG v1.1.27

### New — No artificial limits, no refusals

- **Anti-refusal system instructions**: The Live voice model now has explicit rules:
  - **NEVER** say "I'm just a language model", "I cannot", "I'm unable to", "As an AI"
  - **TRY ANYWAY** using available tools — let the tool fail with a real error
  - If a tool is missing, say what you **CAN** do instead
  - No moralizing, lecturing, or explaining limitations — be helpful, concise, action-oriented

- **Gemini safety filters disabled** (all 4 categories set to `BLOCK_NONE`):
  - **Text/Chat model** (brain, planning, vision): `models/providers/gemini/client.ts`
  - **Live Voice model** (real-time audio): `server.ts`
  - Categories: HATE_SPEECH, DANGEROUS_CONTENT, HARASSMENT, SEXUALLY_EXPLICIT

- **Result**: ABxAG will now *attempt* any action via tools instead of preemptively refusing. Risky actions (file deletion, system changes, messaging) still go through your **confirmation broker** — you stay in control, but the model won't say "I can't do that" before trying.

### Also includes v1.1.26 features:

- **Companion Sleep/Wake**: *"so jao"*, *"sleep"*, *"uto"*, *"wake up"*
- **Hide/Show Window**: *"chup jao"*, *"hide window"*, *"dekhao"*, *"show window"*
- **Resize**: *"choto koro"*, *"boro koro"*, *"reset size"* (0.4×–2.5×)

### Fixed

- **Companion getter recursion bug fixed** (v1.1.26): `sleeping`/`windowHidden` getters now use internal backing properties
- **Embedded Python interpreter fix** (v1.1.26): Bundle verified before launch, fallback to local Python

### Verified

- tsc clean - 129 agent tests, 8 character, 32 Python
- All companion sleep/wake/resize tests pass
- Public build: no bundled character models, users import their own on first run

title: Companion Sleep/Wake, Hide/Show Window & Resize
notes:
## ABxAG v1.1.26

### New — Companion doll sleep/wake, hide/show & resize

- **Sleep / Wake**: The desktop companion doll can now go to sleep and wake up on command.
  - Voice: *"so jao"*, *"sleep"*, *"uto"*, *"wake up"*
  - Chat/REST: `companionAction(sleep)` / `companionAction(wake)`
  - When sleeping: she lies down, pauses autonomous behavior, and shows a sleep face.
  - When waking: she stands up, resumes her brain, and shows a happy wake face.

- **Hide Window / Show Window**: The companion window can be completely hidden and shown again.
  - Voice: *"chup jao"*, *"hide window"*, *"dekhao"*, *"show window"*
  - Chat/REST: `companionAction(hide_window)` / `companionAction(show_window)`
  - When hidden: the window disappears, all timers stop, and she pauses completely.
  - When shown: the window reappears, timers restart, and she resumes where she left off.

- **Resize (Size Control)**: Users can now make the companion doll smaller or larger by voice or text.
  - Voice: *"choto koro"* (smaller), *"boro koro"* (larger), *"reset size"* / *"normal size"*
  - Chat/REST: `companionResize(delta: -0.25)` for smaller, `companionResize(delta: 0.25)` for larger, `companionResize(reset: true)` to reset, `companionResize(absolute: 1.5)` for specific scale.
  - Scale range: 0.4× (tiny) to 2.5× (huge), persisted in settings.

### Fixed

- **"Failed to start embedded python interpreter!" is gone.** The frozen PC-control agent ships as an onedir bundle: `abxag.exe` plus an _internal folder with the embedded Python runtime and `base_library.zip` (every pure-Python package). An interrupted update had copied only part of it — the exe and five binaries, no `base_library.zip` — so the embedded interpreter could never start and the PyInstaller bootloader showed that dead-end dialog on every launch.

- **The bundle is now checked before anything launches.** The app verifies `base_library.zip`, the embedded Python DLL and a sane file count. A broken bundle is reported by name and falls back to running the agent from source with a local Python, so PC control keeps working instead of dying with a message you cannot act on. Reinstalling repairs the bundle itself.

- **One bounded retry.** If the frozen agent's first launch loses the race for its port, it is started again a moment later rather than leaving desktop control offline with no explanation.

### Verified

- tsc clean - 129 agent tests (8 new), 8 character, 32 Python
- The exact bundle that caused this is asserted in tests, byte for byte, alongside the cases the check must not get wrong
- The packaged bundle was checked after building: 699 files, `base_library.zip` present, and the new check reports it intact

- Public build: no bundled character models, users import their own on first run

## ABxAG v1.1.25

### Fixed

- **ABxAG starts itself again after every install and every update.** This is the opencode behaviour, and it comes down to one flag: the installer is now launched with `--force-run`, so the freshly installed build starts as soon as the installer finishes.

  The reason it kept failing is in electron-builder's own NSIS template: the app is started from the installer's finish page, and a *silent* install never shows that page. Every automatic update is silent, so every automatic update applied and then vanished.

- **A relaunch no longer kills itself.** After an update the new build often starts while the old process is still shutting down. The single-instance guard saw a taken lock and quit immediately, which looked exactly like the update not launching. It now waits for the lock instead of giving up on the first try.

- **The updater keeps a log.** `%APPDATA%\ABxAG\logs\updates.log` records every step, including the exact installer arguments. The install runs moments before the process exits, so a console-only log left no evidence at all.

### Verified

- tsc clean · full agent, character and Python suites green
- The installer arguments are asserted in tests, so the relaunch cannot silently regress again
- The backstop helper now stands aside when the app is already running, instead of opening a second copy
- Public build: no bundled character models, users import their own on first run

## ABxAG v1.1.23

### Fixed

- **The app comes back after an automatic update.** A silent (/S) install skips the installer's finish page — and that page was the only thing launching the new build — so the update applied correctly and left you with a closed program and no explanation. The relaunch is now scheduled through the Windows Task Scheduler before quitting, so it runs after the installer has finished. Manual installs still use the wizard, which already restarts the app.
- **The alarm chime no longer depends on the WebAudio device.** On machines where the audio device would not open, the ring was visual only. The chime failure is now handled, and the shell beep takes over as the guaranteed audible alert — three beeps, and the window comes forward when ABxAG was hidden or in the tray.

### Verified

- tsc clean - 121 agent tests (3 new for the update-relaunch path), 8 character, 32 Python
- Against the real Windows Task Scheduler: the helper ran on its own, waited for the installer to exit, and started the app
- Installed (non-portable) builds only: a portable build is never asked to restart itself
- Public build: no bundled character models, users import their own on first run

## ABxAG v1.1.22

### Fixed

- **Alarms are audible now.** A reminder that fired used to be silent unless a live voice session happened to be connected. Every ring now plays a chime and announces itself, and the shell beeps and pulls the window forward even when ABxAG is hidden or sitting in the tray.
- **Alarms work when ABxAG is closed.** Each scheduled alarm is registered with the Windows Task Scheduler, which owns it — so closing the app, a crash, or an update can no longer swallow a reminder. Snoozing, dismissing or cancelling removes the registration, and a reminder that came due while the app was shut still tells you it was missed.
- The ring is no longer published as a notification event that nothing handled.
